subject.title: fix(sqlite): allow verified shared wal backports

question: Should OpenClaw let operators assert that an otherwise version-unsafe shared SQLite library contains the WAL-reset backport, thereby bypassing the fail-closed corruption guard?
rationale: Source inspection can confirm the override is narrowly implemented, but only maintainers can authorize weakening the recently established data-integrity boundary and define the evidence operators must possess.

options.title: Approve a guarded exception
options.body: Retain the shared-only override after adding verification documentation, an active-override warning, and real proof on the reported Red Hat/UBI runtime.

options.title: Keep unconditional fail-closed behavior
options.body: Reject the override and require distributions or operators to supply a runtime whose loaded SQLite version is independently recognized as safe.

recommendation.title: Approve a guarded exception
recommendation.body: Retain the shared-only override after adding verification documentation, an active-override warning, and real proof on the reported Red Hat/UBI runtime.

likelyOwner.reason: Owns the merged SQLite WAL-reset enforcement and its fail-closed shared-library policy.
